failures.criterion: Background work cannot starve requests or the reverse: background work takes connections from limits of its own (spec acceptance line 2)
failures.evidence: api/related_terms.go ensureSearchTermStats (from main's #2397, merged into this branch) runs refreshSearchTermStats on s.deps.Store.Pool, the request pool, on the server's lifetime, after the request that started it has answered and outside admission; its transaction rebuilds the project's whole term statistics (ts_stat over every item) and is bounded only by SearchTermStatsInterval (10 min). The periodic pass (RunSearchTermStatsRefresh) is on the background pool; this per-project refresh is not. Real binary (load stack, head build, /legion/scratch/tmp/infra-592-tester/demo.sh): a person creates a project, a psql session holds that project's totals row, the person creates the project's first issue (201 in 0.34 s); pg_stat_activity then shows `dispatch-requests|active|Lock|insert into search_term_totals ...` at 2, 5 and 10 s after the create answered. Red test: packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/related_terms_test.go TestARefreshTheRelatedCheckStartedHoldsNoRequestPoolConnection (commit 'test(dispatch): red test: the statistics refresh a related-item check starts holds no request-pool connection'): it holds the row from a second process's pool, creates the issue, waits until the refresh waits on the row, and requires database.Pool.Stat().AcquiredConns() == 0. `cd packages/envoy && DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://... go test ./internal/dispatch/api/ -run TestARefreshTheRelatedCheckStartedHoldsNoRequestPoolConnection -count=1` fails 3 of 3 at the head: '1 request-pool connections taken while the statistics refresh the create started waits, want 0'. This is the likely cause of CI envoy-go's failure at 8e87c0d8 (https://github.com/sjawhar/legion/actions/runs/40938335761, job envoy-go): TestTheWriterGateAdmitsAWriteAndRefusesAPinnedRead 'pinned_connection_test.go:216: 1 request-pool connections taken after both requests answered, want 0'; that test creates an issue in a project whose check starts this refresh, then counts the same pool.
